question.text: Two spherical stars <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> have densities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math>, respectively. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> have the same radius, and their masses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> are related by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math>. Due to an interaction process, star <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> loses some of its mass, so that its radius is halved, while its spherical shape is retained, and its density remains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math>. The entire mass lost by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is deposited as a thick spherical shell on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> with the density of the shell being <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> are the escape velocities from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> after the interaction process, the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow><msup><mn>15</mn><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mstyle></msup></mfrac></msqrt></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Given here: RA=RB=R and MB=2MA.

Now, after interaction process, radius of remaining star A is RA'=R2 and its mass is MA'=ρA43πRA23=MA8

Applying conservation of energy,

 -GMA'mRA'+12mvA2=0

Escape velocity of star A is vA=2GMA8×R2=v02

Now, for B, mass collected over B is MB'=MA-MA8=78MA.

Let the radius of star B after interaction becomes r.

Applying mass conservation, 

43πr3-R3ρA=43πR3×78ρA

⇒r=15813R

∴ vB=2G×2MA+78MA151/3R2

=2GMAR216+781513

=v0×23×28×1513=v02×231513

Now, the ratio vBvA=231513=2.30×101513

∴ n=2.30
